methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
OBSIDIA Semiconductor is a seed-stage chip design company founded by Erik Hosler and Adam Wilson, operating within a competitive ecosystem of 12 same-sector peers. The valuation universe includes 3 public semiconductor comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, with notable private competitors including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Standard triangulation methods encounter material constraints. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-filter datapoints—only 0 same-stage peers, 1 adjacent-stage peer, and 0 similar-tier peers exist in the filtered set, falling short of the 3-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring cannot proceed absent the target's revenue figures; while public semiconductors trade at a median 21.0x price-to-sales across the three public tickers, private companies rarely disclose sufficient financial detail to operationalize this multiple.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods reflects genuine data constraints rather than analytical shortcomings. Any valuation synthesis would require either: (1) disclosure of OBSIDIA's revenue or revenue guidance; (2) identification of additional seed-stage semiconductor peers with comparable financial transparency; or (3) alternative methodologies anchored to disclosed metrics (e.g., capital raised, burn rate, or customer concentration). Until such data becomes available, a credible point estimate or range cannot be supported by the evidence at hand.
